motion: Does consciousness fundamentally pervade reality and point toward God?

moves.currentDescription: Brain-consciousness accompaniment does not itself establish the productive relationship between them.
moves.lockedProposition: Brain-consciousness accompaniment does not itself establish the productive relationship between them.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: On the other hand, it's a it's a it's a generally held assumption and it seems probably right. Of course, what it doesn't tell us is anything about the relationship between them except that they seem to accompany one another.

moves.currentDescription: Conscious experience arises along a biological line from metabolism and self-maintenance rather than from computation alone.
moves.lockedProposition: Conscious experience arises along a biological line from metabolism and self-maintenance rather than from computation alone.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: I think this controlled hallucination view that connects with the evolution point, actually. The reason the brains are making best guesses, predicting things, in my view, is closely tied to the function of the brain in keeping the body alive. When you can predict, you can control. And I see this as as going as an imperative that that goes right down to the deeper layers of biology, to things like metabolism and autopoiesis, this idea that living systems create their own material basis. They regenerate their own parts and organization. They don't just transform an input into an output. And so I see a very direct line from distinctive properties of life, metabolism, autopoiesis, to uh what's going on in our brains and bodies that underpins conscious experiences. In short, I think it's life rather than computation that breathes the fire into the equations of consciousness.
